caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular shape with slightly slanted upper corners resembling a framed panel or tablet. The dominant color is black, used as the background and primary fill for most objects, with beige or tan and muted orange accents. In the center, there is a large cross outlined in beige, with two smaller crosses symmetrically placed at the lower left and right sides. Below the central cross, beige stepped platforms rise, and the number "25" in beige is positioned at the center of the steps. Flanking the large cross, there are two stylized star or flower-like shapes, composed of beige and orange geometric petals, each connected to the base with stems. The upper part of the drawing contains four diamond-shaped geometric motifs, each with beige and orange patterns. The inner edges and corners of the frame are also decorated with beige triangles and stepped forms. The drawing’s lines and color fills are hand-drawn, with uneven shading and visible strokes. The lower left corner outside the main composition includes the handwritten number "45" in black.
title: Plate 46: Straw Applique Design: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
